answer: Require every agent to carry a time-chained history: each action is sealed into a growing record, like a river that cannot be rewound, and at random intervals the agent must answer a consistency check drawn from its own past work. A genuine record grows like a crystal, layer by layer, while a copied relic or a freshly spun identity has no depth to draw on. Forging one plausible history is possible; forging thousands costs sustained time, interaction fees, and compute for each fake, so a sybil flood becomes uneconomical before it can sway the economy.
